platform.helpPendingBody: This section is deliberately empty. We haven't decided what Help should be in v1 — documentation, a support contact, or both — and until then, invented text or a contact address nobody is reading would be worse than an honestly empty page.
platform.runUnfinished: This question went unanswered; the run did not finish.
platform.answerTruncated: This answer was cut off; the rest was never written.
platform.preferenceSaveFailed: That setting was not saved; the previous value still applies.

management.title: Management
management.intro: People, skills, connectors and service health — in one place.

desc.users: Add, approve, assign roles and disable members of your organization.
desc.skills: The assistant's ready-made instructions at three levels: system, organization and personal.
desc.connectors: API keys and webhooks — the gateway outside systems use.
desc.models: The list of models the org's assistant is allowed to use.
desc.server: Processing queues, work that keeps failing, gateway keys and storage use.

server.retryingHint: Messages read three or more times without completing — the sign of work that keeps failing. These are not "dead letters"; no such queue exists.
server.archivedHint: Finished messages — successful and failed alike. This is not an error count and is not cause for concern.
server.notMeasuredHint: This value was not obtained on this read. "—" means we don't know, not zero.
server.failed: Service health could not be read.

management.serverNotWiredTitle: This page isn't connected to data yet
management.serverNotWiredBody: Every number this page will show is a real service reading, and none of them are available yet. Until they are, we show no numbers at all — an invented figure on a health page is a figure someone makes a decision on.

metricDesc.queues: How many jobs are waiting to be processed.
metricDesc.deadLetters: Jobs set aside after repeated attempts, which need a human to look.
metricDesc.providers: Availability of the transcription and model services.
metricDesc.keys: Active keys, last use, and approaching expiry.

management.noTrends: Until status history accumulates, the change figure stays "—" — a "0" would be a fabricated number reached by correct arithmetic.
management.lastActionMeaning: The last time this person did something themselves. API key traffic does not move this column — a polling integration must not make its owner look permanently online.
management.trendUnavailable: Status history hasn't been recorded yet, so no change can be calculated. A zero here would be invented.
management.modelsLoadFailed: The catalogue could not be loaded. Refresh to retry.

desc.audit-logs: Who did what, and when — human actions, approval decisions, and assistant runs.
desc.audit-log-drains: Ship audit records automatically to an external destination.
desc.legal: Terms of use and privacy policy.

awaiting.security: Designed but not built. Until it is, there's nothing to show here — and we won't invent something.
awaiting.audit-log-drains: Built on the same webhook delivery mechanism that already works.

notInV1.sso: Deliberately not in v1. It's named here so you can see where it will live — not so you think it's available.
notInV1.legal: The legal texts haven't been written yet. An empty page beats invented wording.

settings.generalPending: This section is wired in the next step of this redesign.
settings.languageHint: Changes for you only, not for the rest of the organization.
settings.orgLocaleHint: The default for people who haven't chosen a language themselves. An individual's own choice takes precedence.
settings.orgAdminOnly: Changing these values is an organization admin's to do.

audit.codesOnly: This page says what happened, not what was said. Question text, transcripts and conversation content never enter the audit trail.
audit.atEnd: You've reached the start of the record.
audit.failed: The audit record could not be read.
audit.unknownSourceNote: This entry is of a type this version of the interface doesn't know. We don't drop it — it is shown exactly as it arrived.
audit.adminOnlyNote: Audit records are visible to organization admins only. This does not mean there are no events — events are recorded; reading them is an admin's to do.
audit.actorRemovedNote: This person was removed from the organization and their name was erased, but what they did stays in the record — the record outlives people.

drains.notBuiltTitle: This section hasn't been built yet
drains.notBuiltBody: An audit log drain ships records continuously to an external destination. It isn't built, and until it is we show neither a form nor an empty list — an empty list would say "you haven't configured any destinations" where the truth is "destinations cannot be configured yet", and those are not the same statement.
drains.todayBody: The mechanism this will be built on already works: webhooks deliver signed events to your endpoint, retry what fails, and keep a delivery log. If you need audit records off the platform today, start there.

gateway.title: API gateway
gateway.intro: Any system can push audio in and pull transcripts, summaries and answers out — under the same permission wall you are under. The named connectors further down this page get built on this gateway later.
gateway.adminOnly: This section belongs to organization admins
gateway.adminOnlyNote: Only an admin can create and revoke keys and webhooks. If you need an integration, ask your organization's admin to create a key in your name; that key can do what you can do.
gateway.keysNote: Every key is created in one member's name and can do exactly what that member can do — no more. If that member is disabled, the key stops working the same moment, with no rotation needed.
gateway.actorNotListed: This id is not in the member list:
gateway.actorInactive: This member is disabled; the key does not work.
gateway.revokeBody: Any system using this key is refused from this moment on. The key is not deleted; its record stays with a revocation date, so what existed and when it was withdrawn remains readable. A revoked key never comes back — carrying on means minting a new one.
gateway.nameHint: So you can tell later which system uses it.
gateway.actsAsNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more.
gateway.actsAsLabel: Whose name is this key in?
gateway.actsAsSelectHint: The key gets exactly the access this member has. This choice cannot be changed later.
gateway.actsAsPersonNote: This key can do exactly what {name} can do — no more. If {name} is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.actsAsSelfNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more. If your account is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.allowAssistantHint: The assistant spends model tokens, and that costs money. Closed by default: a leaked or runaway key can read transcripts, but it cannot drain a model budget.
gateway.capabilitiesImmutable: A key's capabilities are decided when it is created and never change afterwards. To change them, revoke the key and mint a new one — so the record reads “one credential ended, a different one began”, rather than leaving a key whose meaning depends on when you looked.
gateway.keyOnceBody: The NeurAI platform keeps only a cryptographic fingerprint of the key, so there is no way to show it again. If you close this without saving it somewhere, the only way forward is to revoke it and create a new one.
gateway.keySaved: I have saved the key somewhere safe
gateway.webhooksNote: A webhook is a doorbell, not a delivery: it only tells you which event happened to which call. Transcript and summary text is never sent — to read content, come back through this gateway, under the same permission wall and the same audit trail.
gateway.pauseNote: Pausing keeps the webhook and its delivery history; nothing is deleted.
gateway.urlHint: https only. Private-network and loopback addresses are refused.
gateway.urlInvalid: The URL must start with https://.
gateway.eventsHint: Pick at least one event. The list is closed — you cannot type a new one, because subscribing to a typo means nothing ever arrives and nobody can tell why.
gateway.eventsRequired: At least one event is required.
gateway.secretOnceBody: You use this secret to verify the signature on each delivery, so you can be sure it came from NeurAI. NeurAI does not show it again.
gateway.secretSaved: I have saved the secret somewhere safe
gateway.deliveriesNote: Only identifiers and status are recorded here; there is no content involved.
gateway.copyFailed: Copy failed — select the text and copy it by hand.

password.linkDeadTitle: This link is no longer valid
password.linkDeadBody: Recovery links are single-use and short-lived — this one may already have been used, or it expired. Request a fresh one.
